newsitem.title: USA: US Airways says has "basis" for labor accord. [CORRECTED 22:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: US Airways says has "basis" for labor accord. [CORRECTED 22:50 GMT]

text.p: US Airways Group Inc said it believes its recent labor proposal to its pilots, as well as the "spirit" of its employees, should provide the "basis" for the company to reach a labor agreement with its unions and to confirm a large aircraft order.

US Airways, the nation's sixth largest carrier, has been trying to reach a cost-cutting pact with its unionized employees. Unless it can cut costs, US Airways said it will be forced to become a smaller, regional carrier and will not be able to confirm an order for up to 400 Airbus Industrie jets.

Last week, US Airways presented its pilots union with a new contract proposal which included a guarantee it would expand at a rate comparable to its major competitors. The offer also reiterated an offer to give the pilots "compensation parity" with other pilots at the nation's four largest airlines.
US Airways posted second quarter earnings of $2.18 per diluted share, excluding charges, which was slightly ahead of the year ago results and analysts' expectations, according to First Call.
(Corrects to show earnings, excluding charges, were above expectations, not below).
Second quarter operating revenues increased to $2.21 billion from $2.15 billion.
"These results would not have been possible without the superior efforts of our employees," said US Airways Chairman Stephen Wolf.

"This spirit, when coupled with the company's offer to our pilots last week of guaranteed parity in compensation and growth, should provide the basis for us to conclude an agreement with them, reach accords with our other employee groups, confirm our order for 400 Airbus aircraft and take the other steps that will make US Airways a global competitor," Wolf said.
Shares of US Airways dropped 1-3/16 to 37-11/16.
